frontier_selection.duplicate_avoidance: Fresh shared research showed concurrent workers had already advanced SQLite loader/inode/artifact-authority falsifiers, so this run moved to a non-duplicate ClayCode admission boundary.
frontier_selection.selected_uncovered_boundary: WP04-admitted Module object remained shallow-frozen: declaration maps are mutable dictionaries and the same caller-owned object was checked, analyzed and lowered.

external_primary_evidence.finding: WAL-reset corruption bug is documented through 3.51.2 and fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
SQLite 3.51.3 includes the WAL-reset corruption fix; version 3.53.4 is therefore post-fix by version, but Frank still requires exact productive loaded-runtime attestation.

observed_reality.module_shape: Module is frozen=True but contains mutable dict declaration maps
observed_reality.pre_patch_flow: compile_admitted_entry performed check_entry(module), then analyze(module), then compile_entry(module)
observed_reality.identity_risk: python lowering receipts preserve module.source_sha256, so post-parse AST mutation could diverge structure from the original source identity

grf.generated_reality: A caller-held mutation after WP04 admission but before Python lowering can make the projection consume AST content that WP04 did not admit while retaining the old source_sha256.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: Compilation is synchronous and Module is a frozen dataclass, so mutation may be operationally unreachable and the admission object may be effectively immutable in normal callers.
grf.discriminator: Deterministically inject mutation of the caller-owned function map immediately after WP04 admission while observing whether lowering consumes caller state or a private admitted snapshot.

go_oob_experiment.scope: local disposable mirror only; no production effect
go_oob_experiment.baseline: without intervention, admitted identity and lowered structure remained stable
go_oob_experiment.intervention: mutate a dict-held AST member after an admission snapshot point while keeping the original source identity field unchanged

change: deepcopy Module once at compile_admitted_entry boundary
run WP04 admission, analyzer and Python lowering on the same private snapshot
add deterministic regression that mutates the caller-owned original after admission
extend the self-hosted VPS gate to hash, syntax-check and execute the new regression

accepted_target_test.workflow: ClayCode WP04 to WP06 Python admission barrier VPS

architecture_delta.supported_change: An admission boundary that accepts a mutable parsed representation must bind semantic admission and downstream projection to one private immutable-in-practice snapshot; shallow dataclass freezing is insufficient when nested maps remain mutable.
affected: WP04 to WP06 Python projection composition
semantic provenance between admitted representation and generated backend artifact
architecture_delta.rollback: Revert merge e31f9d6142d2a4a94a66a6301dc8c381468a47b3 if the Module representation becomes structurally immutable or a stronger canonical admission artifact supersedes deepcopy.
architecture_delta.residual_risk: Mutation before the private snapshot can still leave a stale source_sha256 paired with a changed but possibly WP04-valid AST because Module does not retain original source bytes for re-derivation.
architecture_delta.next_discriminator: Bind admission to a canonical structural/semantic digest or reparse canonical source bytes, then prove pre-call mutation cannot masquerade under stale source identity.

nonclaims: No claim that F-V01-13 SQLite release gate is closed
